summary: Short comments from Rand on the file transfer proposal in RFC 114. Rand sees a need for such a protocol and finds the proposal simple and extensible. It wants file transfer programs to have full access to local storage, including files they did not create.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 141 records Rand's comments on the file-transfer proposal in RFC 114. The authors support the proposal and suggest additional file operations, status information, and clearer error reports.

subtitle: Rand's comments on file access, commands, status, and errors in RFC 114.

tldr.problem: The file-transfer proposal in RFC 114 needed review from sites considering implementation.
tldr.mechanism: Harslem and Haefner support the proposal and suggest broader file access, record commands, file-name listings, status replies, and more informative error responses.
tldr.outcome: RFC 141 updates RFC 114 with review comments and questions; it is not a replacement specification.

today: RFC 141 updates RFC 114 with review comments. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces it.

sections.title: Support and File Access
sections.content:
Harslem and Haefner say a file-transfer protocol is needed and consider Bhushan's proposal straightforward to implement and extensible.

They would like file-transfer programs to access files that they did not create, where possible. They also suggest commands to insert, delete, and replace records and a way to list files under the user's access control.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors support the proposal and want programs to reach existing files, edit records, and list accessible files.

sections.title: Status and Execution Requests
sections.content:
The authors note that the proposal has no status requests or responses. Because it includes an execute request, they suggest being able to ask about the status of a process it creates, especially if execution waits for scheduling.

For an execute operation, they discuss when parameters should be sent to the remote system. They prefer an approach that starts an independent task and suggest including parameters in the execute command or delaying execution until the parameters arrive.
sections.plainLanguage: If a remote system starts a job, the requester should be able to ask about its status. The authors also discuss how to provide the job's parameters before it starts.

sections.title: Reporting Errors and Sharing Results
sections.content:
For abnormal termination, the authors suggest including part or all of the request that failed along with an identifying code. This would help users recognize the error more precisely.

They also ask for reports on the MIT and Harvard experiments with RFC 114, including any pitfalls discovered. RFC 141 itself does not give those results.
sections.plainLanguage: An error reply should include information that identifies the failed request. The authors also ask early testers to share the problems they found.

references.text: Bhushan, A., "A File Transfer Protocol", RFC 114.
